about.title: Rolling Hills Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Rolling Hills is a small, quiet Los Angeles County community of under 2,000 residents, and most injuries here don't happen on the roadway — public crash records show only a single injury collision in the most recent year. That means when someone in this community is hurt, it's often tied to something else entirely: a faulty piece of equipment, a household appliance, a tool, or a consumer product that didn't perform as it should have. California treats these cases differently than a typical accident claim. Under strict liability principles, an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product itself was defective in its design, manufacturing, or warnings, and that the defect caused harm. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent clients directly. We're a free service that listens to what happened, then connects you with an independent, contingency-based attorney in our network who can evaluate whether a product defect claim fits your situation.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Ease Your Burden
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to prove anyone was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused your injury. An independent attorney can help determine if this standard applies to your case.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers can potentially be held liable for a defective product under California law. We connect you with an attorney who can help identify every party that may bear responsibility.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective product, its packaging, and any related paperwork can be critical to a claim. An independent attorney can advise you on how to safely preserve this evidence while your case is reviewed.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California often allows product liability claims under strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the maker was careless. An independent attorney in our network can review your situation to see how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product exactly as it was at the time of the incident, along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts. Don't attempt repairs or throw anything away. This evidence can be important if an attorney decides to pursue a claim on your behalf.

items.question: Rolling Hills is such a small community — does that affect my claim?
items.answer: Your location doesn't change California product liability law, but a small community can mean fewer local incident reports for reference. Whether your injury happened at home, along Crenshaw Boulevard, or elsewhere in the area, an independent attorney can still evaluate the specifics of what happened to you.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys who work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for you. We don't charge for the connection itself.
